response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same projection. Differences from prior: the prior is displayed with higher contrast and mild rotation, and the current is softer and flatter with no rotation. The current image has a bright band along the top edge (detector or collimation edge). These differences limit comparison of subtle density change at the hila and of small nodules.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None. No finding is flagged time-sensitive. Review priority order: left hilum (F1), left hilar ring lucency (F6), right lower zone markings (F5, F8), cardiac silhouette (F7).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central with the expected slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch. No central airway narrowing at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone (F5) and mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base (F8), without focal consolidation, similar on both studies. Each was recorded by one of the two blind reads only. Some right lower zone haze may be overlying soft tissue. A tiny density over the right medial upper zone is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent aortic knuckle consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior. Upper mediastinum not widened. Right hilum unremarkable. Left hilum: the prior shows a fuller, denser, more lobulated left hilar shadow than the current, which is not bulky and shows an end-on bronchus. Change in the left hilum is INDETERMINATE (F1). It was recorded by one of the two blind reads only, as indeterminate, and the contrast and rotation differences between studies may explain it. The left hilum is fuller and denser than the right on both studies, and a small ring lucency projects over it on the current study, possibly a bronchus end-on (F6). This was recorded by one read only, as stable. The higher prior contrast may account for the denser appearance.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. Left dome level with or slightly higher than the right, with gas-filled stomach and bowel beneath it and no gas under the right dome. Dome relationship matches on both studies. Gas distension under the left dome is INDETERMINATE for change: the two blind reads disagreed (one read stable, one read decreased on the current) (F3).
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal for a PA film, with sharp borders. Similar size and contour on both studies (F7, recorded by one read only).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited. Left-sided central venous catheter with its tip projecting over the expected superior vena cava, same course and tip position as prior, no new device (F2).

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No change confirmed. Left hilum appears smaller on the current in words, but this is indeterminate (F1). Gas distension under the left dome appears less on the current by one read only, and the reads disagreed (F3).
- Unchanged: Right lower zone coarse markings. Aortic knuckle and mediastinal width. Heart size and contour. Left hilar fullness relative to the right (one read only). Catheter course and tip position. Relationship of the diaphragm domes. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum (F1): change from prior is indeterminate. The current left hilum appears smaller and less dense than the prior, but contrast and rotation differences prevent a confident call, and vessel versus node cannot be separated on a frontal film. Only one of two blind reads recorded this.
2. Left hilum (F6): left hilum is fuller and denser than the right on both studies, with a small ring lucency on the current, possibly an end-on bronchus. Not resolved on this film, and recorded by one read only.
3. Right lower zone (F5, F8): mildly coarse markings without focal consolidation, unchanged from prior. Overlying soft tissue may contribute.
4. Heart (F7): cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal, similar to prior.
5. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior. This single frontal film does not show a cause for the breathlessness, and the left hilar question remains unresolved. Triage urgency is high and radiologist review is needed. On-call page is not flagged.
6. Unresolved items are listed under CAN'T DETERMINE, including a possible tiny right upper zone density on the prior only, retrocardiac and left base opacity, catheter tip position and the left-dome gas change (reads disagreed).

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the left hilar question (F1, F6). The findings give no interval, so timing is for the attending to set. Triage urgency is high.
- Lateral view or CT chest for retrocardiac, left base and hidden-area nodule questions.
- Review the source images in PACS, including bone settings and catheter windowing.
- Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging, the surgical history and the line insertion record.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
